# dsh-assist-chat
English | 中文
**Side chat for DeepSeek Harness.** Ask a follow-up without derailing what you are working on.
Opens a second conversation in the right dock that **already knows everything the main thread knows*
* — your current task, the error you just hit, the file you just edited. Ask your question there, ge
t your answer, and the main thread stays exactly as it was.
## The problem it solves
You are mid-task. Something occurs to you that is not part of the task:

- "what does this error actually mean?"
- "would this approach even work?"
- "what is that function

s error actually mean?"
- "would this approach even work?"
- "what is that function supposed to do?"
You have three options today, and two of them are bad:
| Option | Knows your context | Keeps your main thread clean |

| Open a new conversation | ❌ You re-explain everything from scratch | ✅ |
| Just ask in the main th
read | ✅ | ❌ The question and answer get written into the transcript you were about to hand off, and

the agent gets derailed |
| **Side chat** | ✅ It forks the conversation | ✅ Nothing you say reaches

railed |
| **Side chat** | ✅ It forks the conversation | ✅ Nothing you say reaches the main thread |
A side chat is the third option done properly. It is the same idea as the side chat in ZCode: a tab
in the right dock, backed by a real, parallel conversation — not a modal, and it never takes over th
dock, backed by a real, parallel conversation — not a modal, and it never takes over the main area.
## What it feels like

1. You are in a conversation with some history. A **Side chat** button sits in the session header.
2
. Click it. The right dock opens with a tab called **Side chat**, containing a copy of that conversa

tion — every message from before is already there.
3. Ask your question. It answers using the full c

ontext you already built up.
4. Close the tab. Your main conversation never noticed a thing.
From the keyboard, `Ctrl+Shift+B` (`Cmd+Shift+B` on macOS) does the same thing wherever the focus is
, and focuses the tab if it is already open.
The panel is not a reimplementation of chat: it mounts the product own Conversation surface, so stre
aming, markdown, tool cards, approvals, Stop and the composer behave exactly like the main conversat
g, markdown, tool cards, approvals, Stop and the composer behave exactly like the main conversation.
## Features
- **A branch, not a blank slate** — every opening forks the main conversation as it is right now, so

no re-explaining.
- **Genuinely isolated** — its own Session, its own agent, its own transcript. No

thing leaks into the main thread.
- **Native chat surface** — messages, streaming, tool calls, code

blocks, Stop, composer: all inherited, none redrawn.
- **One branch per conversation** — conversatio

n A side chat never appears while you are looking at B.
- **Tab lifecycle is branch lifecycle** — on
e branch while the tab is open (survives tab switches and dock collapse), retired when you close the

tab.
- **No clutter** — the branch is hidden from the left session list while alive, and archived o

nce you close it.
- **Keyboard access** — `Ctrl+Shift+B` (`Cmd+Shift+B` on macOS) opens the side cha
t for the conversation on screen, or focuses it if it is already open. On Desktop it is a normal com
mand you can rebind in the shortcut settings; on the Web build, where the host already owns that cho
rd, the plugin claims it first.
## Roadmap
Directions, not promises — no release date is attached to any of them.
- **Ask about a selection** — highlight text in the main conversation and send it to the side chat a

s quoted context, instead of copying and pasting it.
- **Bring the conclusion back** — insert the si
de chat's conclusion into the main thread as a single quoted message, instead of replaying the whole

side conversation.
- **Several side chats for one conversation** — keep more than one live branch f

rom the same conversation, each in its own tab.
- **Refresh the snapshot** — re-fork the latest main
conversation without closing the tab first.
**0.3.0 and later**

- **Nested side chats** — ask a follow-up from inside a side chat.
- **Save as a real conversation**

— promote a branch into the normal session list when you want to keep it.
- **Choose model and perm
issions** — pick which model and permission mode the branch inherits when it forks, instead of alway
s mirroring the main thread.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Use `--profile web` instead of `--profile desktop` if you run the browser build. **Restart DeepSeek
Harness afterwards** — the button appears in the session header.
## FAQ

**Why can I not find it in the left session list?**
By design. The branch exists as a real Session (
it has to, to have its own agent), but its catalog row is hidden while the tab is open, so your list
stays clean. Close the tab and it is archived.

**Does it see what I say in the main thread afterwards?**
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
*This section is for people reading the source. You do not need it to use the plugin.*
Registered pieces:
| Piece | Registration |
| Tab type | `ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register({ id, kind: "assistchat", keepMounted: true, guide })` |

| Tab body | `ctx.slots.register({ name: "sidebar.right.pane.tab", key: <id>, children })` |
| Chat
surface | `renderFactorySlot("conversation.content", { variant: "embedded", phase, hero }, { slots:

{ views: FixedChatView } })` |
| Entry point | `conversation.session.header.actions` — a list seat;
`.corner` is single and already taken |
Branch lifecycle: resolve the conversation on screen (`uiWorkspace.mainReference.sessionId`) → `sess
ions.fork({ sessionId, increaseTitle: true })` → `sessions.retain(...)` → release and archive on unm
ount. The parent id rides the tab navigation params, so the dock keeps the branch bound to its own c
rent id rides the tab navigation params, so the dock keeps the branch bound to its own conversation.
## Compatibility

- DeepSeek Harness `>= 0.2.0` (`engines.dsh`).
- Client plugin API only: no host-side code, no patch

ed DSH files.
- Tested on 0.2.1-rc.3, desktop profile.
